collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The village and a neighboring settlement want to sing together at a shared festival: blend their songs, or sing back and forth.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The fishing settlement across the bay has invited the village to a shared festival, and the two communities are supposed to sing together. (subject) wants to blend their songs into one. (friend) worries the village's songs will get lost, and wants each side to sing its own, back and forth across the fire. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The two villages spend three evenings blending their songs. The result has the bay's drums and Isola's harmonies, and nobody can tell where one ends. Some people on both sides think something was lost. Most people think something was found.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The two villages sing back and forth across the fire, one song each, until dawn. They never sing the same song, and they never need to. By the end, the children of both villages are mixing up the words on purpose.
